name: Statistics Enhancements
summary: Rank, sort, cargo filter; town, vehicle, station columns; industry totals and marks; problem buttons
description:
Improvements to the statistics window's tables (Lines, Vehicles, Stations, Warehouses, Depots, Towns, Industries) and the buttons that open them. Each feature can be turned off in the mod's Settings (the gear next to the mod when choosing a game's mods). Settings also has a Logging switch, off by default, that writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt) for bug reports.

Rank Column: every table starts with a Rank column showing each row's place in the current order, so you can see where a town or line stands and count rows at a glance. Rows with equal values share a place (1, 2, 2, 4). Only the rows the filters and the search leave are counted. With no column sorted, the rows are numbered as listed.

Sort Largest First: the first click on a column header sorts largest first (most population, most cargo, highest balance), instead of smallest first. Names and other text columns still sort A to Z first, and the Towns tab's rating gauges (reputation, traffic, happiness, delivery, noise, pollution) sort worst first, so the towns with a problem come to the top. Click the header again for the other order.

Scroll to Top on Sort: whenever you sort a table, it jumps back to its first row.

Cargo Filter: the Towns and Industries tabs get a cargo list next to the eye. In the Towns tab, pick a cargo to see only the towns that demand it; in the Industries tab, only the industries that need it, use it as a booster or make it. All Cargo shows them all again. It works together with the eye and the search, and keeps your choice until you quit the game.

Town - Column Enhancements: two changes to the Towns tab's columns. Cargo: the Towns tab shows one figure each for Supply, Demand and Coverage, summed over all cargos, and the cargos as a row of icons, so you can't tell which cargo a town lacks. With this mod the four columns become two. Demand shows each cargo the town wants with its amount, largest first. Supply shows each cargo your lines supply with its amount, coloured by the share of its demand met as the town window rates supplies: green from 67%, yellow from 33%, red below. Hover a figure for the cargo's supply of its demand and the exact share in each district (residential, commercial, industrial), and for the whole town when more than one district wants it. Demand sorts by the town's total demand, Supply by the share of all demand met, as the game's Coverage column did. Public Transport: the Towns tab's Public Transport figure keeps the game's number but is coloured by the town's public transport coverage, the passenger row of the town window's Supplies tab: green from 67%, yellow from 33%, red below, as the town window colours it. Hover the figure for the coverage as the town window gives it ("Public transport coverage is 59%." and "668/1,127"). The number itself is a different figure, the game's public transport reachability of commercial and industrial places, so it doesn't match the town window's passenger supply.

Vehicle - Column Enhancements: the Vehicles tab shows Line before Vehicle, with more room for line names; a name too long for its column shows in full on hover. Before Balance come Income and Running Costs from the vehicle window's Balance card, over the same last 12 months, so Income minus Running Costs is the Balance. The last column is the vehicle's running cost a year at today's rate, as shown at the foot of the vehicle window. Condition is coloured like the vehicle window's condition bar: green, yellow or red.

Station - Column Enhancements: the Stations tab shows each station terminal by terminal. A Terminals column with the terminal count comes first, then Type with the kinds of terminals and their count (a person icon for passenger terminals, a half-person, half-cargo icon for terminals taking both, a cargo icon for any cargo, and each cargo class as a pill in its own colour with the count inside, like the station window: Goods x2, Bulk x1), then Lines with how many of your lines stop at each terminal. After Utilization, a column shows the waiting hall and then each terminal's waiting passengers and capacity, an overcrowded terminal in the station window's warning colour. Their capacities add up to Utilization's, but the game's Utilization counts only the passengers waiting at the terminals, not those in the waiting hall. Delay shows each terminal's unhappy passengers. As many terminals show as fit in the column; the rest are listed on hover. Both sort by the most at any one terminal, so a station with 60 waiting at one terminal comes before one with 30 at each of two. A name too long for its column shows in full on hover. With Line Enhancements, its Assign Lines button stays at the right of the Lines column.

Industry - Recipe Totals: for industries with more than one recipe, the statistics window's Industries tab counts each cargo once in its Input and Output columns. The game counts a cargo once per recipe that uses it, and takes later recipes' figures from the first. Workload compares the input with what the largest recipe takes when it runs all the time, since an industry runs one recipe at a time. Industries with one recipe and no booster show the same figures as before.

Industry - Problem Marks: the statistics window's Industries tab shows nothing about an industry's own troubles. With this mod its Problems column marks two of them with the problem icon. Blocked expansion: when an industry can't grow because something is in the way, its window says "Industry is blocked from further expansion."; hover the mark for that message and click it to open the industry, which shows the blocked area on the map. The mark goes away once the way is clear, just as the industry window's message does. Cargo destroyed: your lines pick up a cargo, but too slowly, so the industry's full output stock destroys part of it: some was shipped in the last year, yet 5% or more of what was made was destroyed, and the output stock has been full in the last two months (so an industry whose stock filled up before your first pickup isn't marked once the pickups keep it below full). Hover the mark for each such cargo, how much was made, destroyed and shipped. A cargo nobody picks up doesn't count: a livestock farm whose meat you collect and whose wool you don't destroys its wool, and that is no problem. Sort by the column to list the marked industries together.

Problem Buttons: the statistics buttons in the game bar turn red while their table has something to look at, so you see at a glance where to check. Every table with a Problems column counts the elements with a problem notification, as that column shows them. The Vehicles button also counts vehicles in very bad condition, the Depots button depots and maintenance buildings whose maintenance pool is full while vehicles in their maintenance area are maintained nowhere and wear down (the box says how many, and how many vehicles the pool served in the last 30 days), the Stations button stations where passengers pile up: a terminal the station window marks as overcrowded, more passengers waiting for a line at a stop than all of that line's vehicles seat together, so the line needs more vehicles, or at least 10 unhappy passengers who make up 30% of those waiting (the Delay column), each only once it lasts, not for a passing moment (the box gives the figures and the worst line), the Warehouses button warehouses where a cargo fills 85% of the room it has (its slots and the empty slots that take it), so there is time to act before it is full, and the Industries button industries blocked from further expansion (the industry window's "Industry is blocked from further expansion."), which the game shows nowhere else, and industries destroying a cargo your lines ship too slowly: some was shipped in the last year, yet 5% or more of what was made was destroyed in the full output stock, and that stock has been full in the last two months (a cargo nobody picks up, such as a farm's wool while only its meat is collected, doesn't count). Point at a red button and a box opens above the button bar with everything it found: a tab per kind with its count, and for each element its name and its figures in columns: a problem notification's type, a worn vehicle's line and condition, an overcrowded terminal's number, lines and waiting passengers, each line with more waiting than its vehicles seat, a station's unhappy passengers of all waiting, a warehouse cargo's icon, storage buildings, stored and room, and fill, a depot's pool, a blocked industry's plots, each cargo an industry destroys with what was shipped, what was destroyed and its share of what was made. Click a name to open that element's window; the locate pin before each name, and before a line named among the figures, moves the camera there. A long list scrolls. The buttons' tooltips stay as in the game. The checks cost next to nothing in frame rate; a button follows a change within a few seconds, a blocked industry within about half a minute.

params.name: Rank Column
params.tooltip: A Rank column first in every statistics table: each row's place in the current order.

params.name: Sort Largest First
params.tooltip: The first click on a statistics column header sorts largest first; names still sort A to Z first, the Towns tab's rating gauges worst first.

params.name: Scroll to Top on Sort
params.tooltip: Sorting a statistics table shows it from its first row.

params.name: Cargo Filter
params.tooltip: A cargo list next to the eye in the statistics Towns and Industries tabs: it shows only the towns that demand the chosen cargo, and only the industries that need, boost with or make it.

params.name: Town - Column Enhancements
params.tooltip: The statistics Towns tab shows Demand and Supply per cargo: each cargo's demand, and each supplied cargo's amount, coloured by the share of its demand met. The Public Transport figure is coloured by the town's public transport coverage (the town window's passenger supply): green from 67%, yellow from 33%, red below.

params.name: Vehicle - Column Enhancements
params.tooltip: The statistics Vehicles tab shows the line first, with room for its name, Income and Running Costs before Balance, each vehicle's running cost a year at the end, and Condition in its condition colour.

params.name: Station - Column Enhancements
params.tooltip: The statistics Stations tab shows each station terminal by terminal: the terminal count, the kinds of terminals with their counts, lines per terminal, waiting passengers and capacity per terminal, and unhappy passengers per terminal in Delay.

params.name: Industry - Recipe Totals
params.tooltip: For industries with more than one recipe, the statistics Industries tab counts each cargo once in Input and Output, and Workload compares against the largest recipe.

params.name: Industry - Problem Marks
params.tooltip: The statistics Industries tab's Problems column marks industries blocked from further expansion and industries destroying cargo they ship too slowly (some shipped and some destroyed in the last year, the output stock full in the last two months; a cargo nobody picks up doesn't count); click a mark to open the industry.

params.name: Problem Buttons
params.tooltip: The game bar's statistics buttons turn red while their table has a problem: a problem notification, a vehicle in very bad condition, a full maintenance pool while vehicles in its maintenance area go unmaintained and wear down, an overcrowded station, more passengers waiting for a line than all its vehicles seat, or many unhappy passengers at a station, a warehouse cargo at 85% of the room it has, an industry blocked from expanding, or an industry destroying cargo it ships too slowly. Point at a red button for a box listing them in columns, a tab per kind; click a name to open its window, its pin to look at it.

params.name: Logging
params.tooltip: Writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt), for bug reports.
